terms.grammar: ablative absolute with abesse: “to be away from school, the parents not knowing”
terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase: īnscius, not knowing, and abesse, to be away. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: Lewis & Short: inscius · Lewis & Short: absum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 30, 31, 329.
